name: Vīraśaiva / Liṅgāyata
regions: Kāśī and Kedāra (seats of two of the five pīṭhas)

tradition.text: two accounts: (a) beginningless (anādi) dharma taught by Śiva in the Āgamas and renewed in every age by the five ācāryas; (b) begun by Basava and the śaraṇas in twelfth-century Kalyāṇa

scholarly.text: 12th-c. devotional movement in Karnataka with earlier Śaiva antecedents; Sanskrit systematization and anthologies 14th–16th c.; living community

transmissions_received.what: the Śaiva Āgamas 'from Kāmika to Vātula' as scripture, read as teaching Vīraśaiva dharma in their later portion
institutional continuity of Śaiva maṭhas and sites in Karnataka
transmissions_received.evidence: scholarly hypothesis only (see brw:kalamukha-to-virasaiva); not part of either tradition-account

transmissions_received.what: veneration of the Tamil Nāyaṉmārs as purātanas (ancient devotees)
transmissions_received.evidence: tradition-account: Harihara's ragaḷes and the Basava Purāṇa narrate the purātanas

transmissions_received.what: the vocabulary of full I-ness (pūrṇāhantā) and this-ness (idantā)

distinctive_positions: Śiva is worshipped as the liṅga, and every initiate wears a personal liṅga (iṣṭaliṅga) on the body for life, worshipping it on the palm rather than in temples.

The path runs through six stages (ṣaṭsthala: bhakta, māheśvara, prasādi, prāṇaliṅgi, śaraṇa, aikya) to the union of the soul (aṅga) with the liṅga (liṅgāṅga-sāmarasya); the Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi elaborates them as 101 sthalas.
Guru, liṅga and jaṅgama (the moving devotee-teacher) are one; the eight shields (aṣṭāvaraṇa) and five codes (pañcācāra) govern life.
Work is worship (kāyaka) and its fruit is to be shared (dāsōha).
Initiation is open to all irrespective of caste and sex; the vacanas reject caste, the five pollutions (pañcasūtaka), Vedic sacrifice and temple ritualism.

The vacanas — spontaneous utterances of experience (anubhava) — are scripture for the śaraṇa strand; the Āgamas, the Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi and Śrīpati's Śrīkarabhāṣya are scripture for the Pañcācārya strand.
Death is union with the liṅga (liṅgaikya): the dead are buried, not cremated, and no ancestral rites are needed.
The two strands hold different accounts of the tradition's origin and different views on its relation to the Veda and to 'Hinduism' (recorded as internal debates, not settled here).
summary: The Vīraśaiva or Liṅgāyata tradition of Karnataka and neighbouring regions worships Śiva as the liṅga, worn by every initiate on the body. Its śaraṇa strand looks to Basava, Allama Prabhu, Akka Mahādēvi, Cennabasava and the twelfth-century vacana saints of Kalyāṇa; its Pañcācārya strand looks to five ācāryas who emerged from liṅgas in every age and to the Sanskrit Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi. Both teach the six stages to union with Śiva, the unity of guru, liṅga and jaṅgama, work as worship and the equality of devotees.
notes: family 'vedic' follows the coverage-map grouping (A7); whether the tradition stands within or outside the Vedic/Hindu fold is itself a recorded internal debate (dsp:lingayata-hindu-identity).

name: Pañcācārya (Pañcapīṭha) tradition

tradition.text: the five ācāryas appear in every yuga from liṅgas; in the Kali age as Revaṇa (Reṇuka), Maruḷa, Ēkōrāma, Paṇḍitārādhya and Viśvārādhya

scholarly.text: the five-pīṭha organization and its Sanskrit literature are attested from the late medieval period; dates debated

distinctive_positions: Vīraśaiva dharma is beginningless (anādi), taught by Śiva in the later portion of the Śaiva Āgamas (SSM 5.14) and consistent with the Veda (SSM 5.5–13).
Basava is honoured as a great devotee and reviver within this older stream, not as its founder.
The Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi's 101 sthalas are the full map of the path; doctrine is Śivādvaita (SSM 3.86) — in Śrīpati's formulation, Śakti-viśiṣṭādvaita.
Five pīṭhas (seats), each founded by one ācārya, transmit initiation through the guru lineage.
summary: The strand of Vīraśaivism organized around five ācāryas — Revaṇa (Reṇuka), Maruḷa, Ēkōrāma, Paṇḍitārādhya and Viśvārādhya — who, in the tradition's account, emerged from liṅgas at five sacred sites and founded the five pīṭhas. Its scripture is the Śaiva Āgamas read in their Vīraśaiva portion, the Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi and Śrīpati's Śrīkarabhāṣya.
notes: The commentary on the Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi (Tattvapradīpikā) already speaks of the 'world-famous Pañcācārya lineage' (e-text M00207, ch. 6 commentary). Seat names (siṃhāsana) are recorded on the teacher entries at low confidence.

name: Śaraṇa–vacana tradition

tradition.text: founded by Basava and the śaraṇas of Kalyāṇa in the 12th c.

scholarly.text: 12th-c. movement; its literature compiled 15th–16th c.; revived through the printing of the vacanas from the 1920s

distinctive_positions: The vacanas of the śaraṇas, spoken from experience (anubhava), are the tradition's scripture.
Basava (with Allama Prabhu presiding over the Anubhava Maṇṭapa) inaugurated the tradition in Kalyāṇa.
Caste, the five pollutions, Vedic sacrifice and temple worship are rejected; all initiates, women included, are equal.
Work as worship (kāyaka) and sharing its fruit (dāsōha) are the social form of devotion.
Renunciant (virakta) maṭhas carry the teaching; many of its writers regard the Pañcācārya account of origins as later.
summary: The strand of the tradition that looks to Basava and the twelfth-century śaraṇas of Kalyāṇa — Allama Prabhu, Akka Mahādēvi, Cennabasava, Siddharāma and some two hundred vacanakāras of every occupation — and holds their vacanas as scripture. It is carried by the Virakta maṭhas and by the modern vacana revival.

name: Ārādhya Śaiva (Andhra)
distinctive_positions: Wear the liṅga and worship Śiva exclusively while retaining the sacred thread and Vedic rites.
Look to Mallikārjuna Paṇḍitārādhya, contemporary of Basava, as their founding teacher.
summary: A Telugu-speaking Vīraśaiva group, traditionally brāhmaṇa, tracing itself to Mallikārjuna Paṇḍitārādhya; it combines liṅga-wearing and exclusive Śiva devotion with retention of Vedic rites and the sacred thread.
notes: Low confidence on current practice details; recorded as a side in dsp:virasaiva-veda-agama-authority.
